decisions.reason: Accepting Inter and the thicker body-text treatment does not change the requirement to eliminate white space at article endings or the approved filler-asset option.
The body-font decision does not change category content, label placement, category mappings, or the requirement to display category labels.
The accepted font treatment does not modify the required two-page spread behavior or even-page-count constraint.
The typography decision does not alter the requirement for accurate final article page numbers on the cover.
The source confirms body typography only and does not change the table-of-contents completion condition or page-number basis.
The accepted article-body font does not change author-name, author-photo, identity-matching, source, or placement requirements.
The source decision concerns body text and does not modify the required size or circular shape of author photos.
The body-font choice does not affect the prohibition on red in the Dorian Vale article or the reservation of red for the cover.
The accepted body typography has no necessary effect on advertisement clarity, sizing, trim, or bleed quality.
Changing article-body typography does not alter which cover-mentioned articles must be included or how their placement is determined.
The body-font decision does not change the Civic Lantern website as the source of article content.
Approval of a specific body-font treatment does not modify or replace the existing polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement.
